title: Bumblebees Soak Up Far More Toxic Metal Than Honeybees — Even in the Same Field
hook: Foraging in identical patches of flowers, bumblebees pick up two to seven times more toxic heavy metals than honeybees. The gap comes down to biology and lifestyle, not location.
key_points: Bumblebees accumulate 2–7 times more heavy metals in the pollen they collect than honeybees foraging in the same areas, and roughly 3 times higher concentrations in their bodies.
The metals studied include arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt, lead, and tin.
Underground nesting exposes bumblebees to soil contamination that above-ground honeybee hives avoid.
Smaller bumblebee colonies (50–500 bees vs. 30,000–60,000), shorter foraging ranges, fewer visited plant species, and hairier bodies all concentrate their metal exposure further.
Even low-level exposure can quietly impair foraging, learning, navigation, and reproduction, harming colony success over time.
content_html: Put a honeybee and a bumblebee in the exact same flower-filled field, and you'd expect them to pick up roughly the same pollution. They don't. Bumblebees accumulate two to seven times more toxic heavy metals — arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt, lead, and tin — in the pollen they collect, and about three times higher concentrations in their own bodies.
extra_html: The gap comes down to biology and lifestyle rather than location. Bumblebees nest underground, putting them in direct contact with contaminated soil in a way honeybees' above-ground hives avoid. Their colonies are also far smaller — 50 to 500 bees, compared to a honeybee hive's 30,000 to 60,000 — which concentrates whatever exposure occurs across fewer individuals. Bumblebees forage closer to the nest, visit a narrower range of plant species, and have hairier bodies that trap more airborne metal-laden dust. None of this shows up as an acute poisoning; the danger is subtler. Researchers note that even low-level metal exposure can quietly interfere with learning, memory, navigation, and reproduction — the everyday skills a bee colony depends on to survive.

related.title: A 'Safer' Pesticide May Be Quietly Sabotaging Bumblebee Reproduction
related.hook: Sulfoxaflor was designed to spare bees while killing crop pests. Low doses of it are instead altering gene activity in bumblebee ovaries — with signs of fewer offspring to come.

related.title: Some Bees Have Nowhere to Hide From Heat
related.hook: A big study of Australian native bees found that where a bee nests — in plant stems versus underground — may decide whether it survives a warming world.

related.title: Every Bee Flies Its Own Highway
related.hook: Tracked by drone in the wild, individual honey bees turned out to follow their own personal flight paths — sometimes retracing a route to within centimeters.

flashcards.prompt: How much more heavy metal do bumblebees pick up than honeybees foraging in the same area?
flashcards.back_html: 2 to 7 times more in the pollen they collect, and roughly 3 times higher concentrations in their own bodies — despite foraging in identical locations.

flashcards.prompt: Why does underground nesting make bumblebees more exposed to toxic metals than honeybees?

choices.text: It puts them in direct contact with contaminated soil, unlike honeybees' above-ground hives
Underground nests are colder, which concentrates metals chemically
It has no effect — the difference comes only from diet

flashcards.explanation_html: Bumblebees nest underground, exposing them to soil-borne contamination that honeybees, which build hives above ground, largely avoid.

flashcards.prompt: Besides nesting location, what else concentrates bumblebees' metal exposure compared to honeybees?

choices.text: Smaller colonies, shorter foraging ranges, fewer plant species visited, and hairier bodies that trap dust
Bumblebees only eat metal-rich soil directly
Bumblebees live twice as long as honeybees

flashcards.explanation_html: Bumblebee colonies are far smaller (50–500 vs. 30,000–60,000 bees), forage closer to the nest, visit fewer plant species, and have hairier bodies — all factors that concentrate whatever contamination is present.
